mission_04: Isolation Forest is a tree-based anomaly detection algorithm that isolates observations by randomly selecting a feature and then randomly selecting a split value between the maximum and minimum values of the selected feature. The key insight is that anomalies are few and different, so they require fewer random splits to be isolated. Normal points require more splits because they are surrounded by similar points. The algorithm builds an ensemble of isolation trees and computes an anomaly score based on the average path length across all trees. Points with short average path lengths are flagged as anomalies. Isolation Forest is efficient (linear time complexity), works well in high dimensions, and does not assume any specific data distribution, making it one of the most popular anomaly detection algorithms in practice.
